When will I use this?

Trigonometry: when will I use this?

Whenever an angle and a length have to agree.

Toolmaker

Engineering and manufacturing

\(\displaystyle h = L \sin\theta\)

L is the sine bar's length

How do you tilt a part to exactly 10°?

A sine bar sets a part at an exact angle. Its rollers are a fixed distance apart, and a stack of gauge blocks under one roller makes the angle: height = length × sin θ.

  1. A 100 mm sine bar at 10°: \(100 \times \sin 10^\circ = 17.365\) mm of blocks.
  2. A 200 mm sine bar at 25°: \(200 \times \sin 25^\circ = 84.52\) mm.

The answer: \(100 \times \sin 10^\circ = 17.365\) mm

CNC programmer

Engineering and manufacturingHigher

\(\displaystyle (x, y) = (r\cos\theta,\ r\sin\theta)\)

r is the circle's radius

Where exactly do the bolt holes go?

Uses example figures: the numbers marked (example figure) or (example figures) are made up to show the method.

Bolt holes on a circle (a pitch circle) are programmed as coordinates: x = r cos θ, y = r sin θ. Three holes 120° apart on a circle of radius 50 mm (example figures):

  1. At 0°: (50, 0).
  2. At 120°: x = \(50 \times \cos 120^\circ = -25\), y = \(50 \times \sin 120^\circ = 43.301\).

The answer: \(50 \times \cos 120^\circ = -25\) mm

Crime scene investigator

Protective services

\(\displaystyle \sin\theta = \dfrac{\text{width}}{\text{length}}\)

What angle did this blood drop hit at?

Uses example figures: the numbers marked (example figure) or (example figures) are made up to show the method.

A blood drop that hits a surface at an angle leaves a stretched mark. The width ÷ the length is the sine of the angle it hit at. A mark 2 mm wide and 4 mm long (example figures):

  1. sin θ = \(2 \div 4 = 0.5\), so θ = \(\sin ^{-1}(0.5) = 30^\circ \).
  2. A mark 1 mm by 4 mm: \(\sin ^{-1}(0.25) = 14.5^\circ \), a shallower hit.

The answer: \(\sin ^{-1}(2 \div 4) = 30^\circ \)

Practise it

Games on MaffsGames that practise trigonometry:

  • Trig Wars: Set the angle and power of a shot and watch the trigonometry resolve it into horizontal and vertical parts.
  • Trig Worms: Use SOH CAH TOA to find the side or angle that aims the cannon.
  • Trig Identity Duel: Exact trig values, the sine rule and the cosine rule.
  • Whose Side Are You On?: Label the hypotenuse, opposite and adjacent from the marked angle, then link them to sin, cos and tan.
